title: Bai pong moan (Khmer egg and rice)
steps: Beat the eggs with half of the spring onions, a splash of soy sauce and the pepper.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and pour in the eggs, tilting the pan so they spread thinly.
Cook for about 2 minutes until the underside is crisp and golden, then fold the omelette in half and cook for another minute.
Divide the warm rice into four bowls and slice the omelette over it.
Season with the remaining soy sauce or fish sauce, then top with the rest of the spring onions and coriander. Serve with chilli sauce.

title: Cha huoy teuk (jelly dessert with coconut cream and shaved ice)

ingredients.name: mung beans, cooked until soft and sweetened lightly
palm sugar, simmered with 100 ml water into a syrup

steps: Whisk the agar into the cold water, bring to a boil, and simmer for 3 minutes until fully dissolved. Stir in the sugar and pandan extract.
Pour into a shallow tray and chill until firm, then cut into small cubes. Repeat with different colours if you like.
Cook the mung beans in water until soft, drain, and toss with a spoon of sugar. Cook the tapioca pearls separately until clear.
Spoon the jelly, mung beans and tapioca into four tall glasses.
Top with shaved ice, drizzle with coconut cream and palm sugar syrup, and serve right away with a long spoon.

title: Cha kroeung (beef stir-fried with lemongrass paste)

ingredients.name: Thai basil leaves and kaffir lime leaf, to garnish

steps: Pound or blend the lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, lime leaves, 2 cloves of garlic and the shallots into a rough yellow paste (kroeung).
Mix half of the paste with the beef and 1 tbsp of the fish sauce and marinate for 30 minutes.
Blanch the long beans in boiling water for 1 minute and drain.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok until very hot and sear the beef in two batches for about 2 minutes each, then remove.
Fry the remaining paste, the last clove of garlic and the onion in the remaining oil for 2 minutes, then add the pepper and beans and stir-fry briefly.
Return the beef with the palm sugar and remaining fish sauce, toss over high heat for 1 minute, and finish with basil. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Chek ktis (banana and tapioca pearls in coconut milk)

ingredients.name: small ripe bananas, cut into chunks

steps: Boil the tapioca pearls in plenty of water for 10 to 12 minutes until mostly translucent, then drain and rinse.
Heat the coconut milk, water, sugar, salt and the pandan leaf in a pot until the sugar dissolves, and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Add the bananas and the tapioca and cook for 5 minutes, until the pearls are clear and the banana is tender but not collapsing.
Remove the pandan leaf and taste, adding a little more sugar or salt if needed.
Serve warm or chilled, sprinkled with sesame seeds.

title: Chha kh'nhei (chicken stir-fried with ginger and black pepper)

ingredients.name: boneless chicken thighs, in bite-sized pieces
dried wood ear mushrooms, soaked and torn (optional)

steps: Marinate the chicken with half the fish sauce, half the black pepper and the sugar for 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok and fry the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the ginger and cook for a minute.
Add the chicken and stir-fry over high heat for 5 to 6 minutes until browned and nearly cooked.
Add the onion and mushrooms with the oyster sauce, the remaining fish sauce and 3 tbsp water, and cook for 3 more minutes.
Stir in the spring onions and the rest of the pepper, then serve straight away with steamed rice.

title: Chha trob (charred eggplant with minced pork and fermented soybeans)

ingredients.name: fermented soybean paste (or yellow bean sauce)
black pepper and steamed rice, to serve

steps: Char the whole eggplants over a gas flame, on a grill or under a very hot oven grill, turning, until the skin is blackened and the flesh is soft, about 10 minutes.
Cool them slightly, peel off the skin, and halve or slice the flesh lengthwise.
Heat the oil in a wok and fry the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the pork and stir-fry over high heat until browned and cooked through.
Stir in the soybean paste, oyster sauce, sugar and 3 tbsp water and cook for 2 minutes until it becomes a thick, glossy sauce.
Arrange the eggplant on a plate, spoon the pork mixture over it, and top with spring onions and black pepper. Serve with rice.

title: Kampot pepper crab (crab with fresh green peppercorns)

ingredients.name: medium crabs (about 1.2 kg in total), cleaned and cut into pieces
fresh green peppercorns (or 1.5 tbsp coarsely crushed black pepper)
lime juice, salt and pepper dipping sauce, to serve

steps: Crack the crab claws lightly so the flavours get in, and pat the pieces dry.
Heat the oil in a large wok and fry the garlic and shallots for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the crab pieces and stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes until the shells turn bright red.
Add the green peppercorns, fish sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and 4 tbsp water, cover, and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, tossing once or twice, until the crab is cooked through.
Uncover for the last minute to reduce the sauce, add the spring onions, and serve with steamed rice and a dish of lime juice mixed with salt and pepper.

title: Kuyteav (Phnom Penh pork noodle soup)

ingredients.name: minced pork, rolled into small balls
garlic, sliced and fried until golden
lime wedges, fresh herbs and chilli to serve

steps: Blanch the pork bones in boiling water for 5 minutes, drain and rinse them, then return them to a clean pot with the 2.5 litres of fresh water, the onion and the daikon.
Simmer gently for 1.5 hours, skimming off any scum, then season the broth with fish sauce and sugar and strain it.
Soak the rice noodles in warm water for 15 minutes, then cook them briefly in boiling water until tender and divide among four bowls.
Drop the pork meatballs into the simmering broth for 4 minutes, adding the sliced pork for the final minute until just cooked through.
Ladle the hot broth, pork and meatballs over the noodles.
Top with spring onions, fried garlic and bean sprouts, and serve with lime, herbs and chilli at the table.

title: Nataing (pork and coconut dipping curry with rice crackers)

ingredients.name: rice crackers, cucumber and raw vegetables, to serve

steps: Blend the shallots, garlic, chillies, lemongrass and galangal into a thick paste.
Fry the paste in 1 tbsp of the thick top of the coconut milk for 3 minutes, until the oil separates.
Add the pork and break it up with a spoon, cooking for 5 minutes until no longer pink.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, fish sauce, palm sugar and tamarind, and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring, until thick and reduced to a spoonable dip.
Stir in the peanuts and serve warm with rice crackers, cucumber slices and fresh vegetables for dipping.

title: Nhoam svay (green mango salad with dried shrimp)

ingredients.name: firm green mangoes, peeled and cut into matchsticks
dried shrimp, soaked in warm water for 10 minutes and chopped

steps: Whisk the lime juice, fish sauce, palm sugar and garlic until the sugar dissolves, and adjust for a balance of sour, salty and sweet.
Toss the mango, carrot and onion together in a large bowl.
Toast the soaked dried shrimp in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant and slightly crisp.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss well, then fold in the shrimp, chilli and herbs.
Scatter with crushed peanuts and serve immediately as a starter or alongside rice.

title: Num kom (steamed rice cakes with coconut filling)

ingredients.name: warm water, plus a little more if needed
banana leaf pieces, about 20 cm square

steps: Mix the rice flour with the warm water and salt and knead into a soft, smooth dough that does not stick to your fingers.
Combine the coconut, palm sugar and sesame seeds for the filling.
Divide the dough into 12 balls, flatten each one, spoon on a little filling and seal it inside.
Soften the banana leaves over a flame, brush with oil, and wrap each ball in a pyramid-shaped parcel, tucking the ends under.
Steam the parcels over boiling water for 25 minutes until the dough is chewy and translucent.
Let them cool slightly and serve in their leaves, warm or at room temperature.

title: Samlar kako (Cambodian stirring stew with roasted rice)

ingredients.name: green kroeung paste (lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaf, garlic, shallot and turmeric)
rice, dry-toasted until deep golden and ground (roasted rice powder)
fish sauce, plus 1 tsp prahok if you can find it
water spinach or morning glory, chopped
Thai basil and sawtooth coriander (or mint)

steps: Pound or blend the kroeung ingredients into a green paste and fry 3 tbsp of it in a little oil in a heavy pot for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and brown it lightly, then pour in the water and bring to a boil. Simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Stir in the fish sauce, the optional prahok and the palm sugar, then add the pumpkin and eggplants and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the long beans and water spinach and cook for 5 minutes more.
Sprinkle in the roasted rice powder a spoonful at a time, stirring constantly, until the soup thickens slightly and tastes nutty.
Finish with lime juice and the fresh herbs, taste for seasoning, and serve with steamed rice.

title: Saraman curry (beef and peanut coconut curry)
steps: Dry-toast the coriander, cumin, star anise, cloves, cinnamon and cardamom until fragrant, then grind them to a powder.
Pound or blend the chillies, lemongrass, galangal, shallots, garlic and 1 lime leaf with the ground spices into a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in the thick top of the coconut milk for 5 minutes until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add the beef and brown it for 5 minutes, then pour in the rest of the coconut milk and the water and simmer, covered, for 1 hour 15 minutes until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the potatoes, peanuts, tamarind, palm sugar, fish sauce and the remaining lime leaves, and simmer for 25 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the sauce is thick.
Taste for balance and serve with steamed rice.
